method: web research (evidence-backed). Each node carries a usage tier + evidence + source URLs. Anchored on primary Microsoft CEIP telemetry (Jensen Harris, Office UI blog) corroborated by GranneBlog; long tail graded from education/'essential skills' sources + the telemetry's fast-flattening usage curve.

sources.title: No Distaste for Paste (Why the UI, Part 7) — Jensen Harris, Microsoft Office UI Blog
sources.claim: Microsoft CEIP telemetry: top-5 most-used Word 2003 commands are Paste, Save, Copy, Undo, Bold (~32% of all command use); Paste alone >11% and the most-clicked toolbar button; Change Font Size is #11; the usage curve flattens sharply after the top ~10.

sources.title: The most popular commands in Word — GranneBlog
sources.claim: Corroborates the CEIP ranking (Paste, Save, Copy, Undo, Bold top five; Change Font Size #11) as real usage data.

sources.title: How to Format Text in Word (Fonts, Sizes, Styles)
sources.claim: Treats font, size, bold/italic/underline, color/highlight, alignment, line spacing, and Styles as the foundational everyday formatting set; calls Styles 'one of the most powerful formatting tools in Word.'

sources.title: How to use the Format Painter — Nuts & Bolts Speed Training
sources.claim: Format Painter is a widely relied-upon time-saver, but a convenience feature below the core clipboard/emphasis commands.

sources.title: Structuring Documents in Microsoft Word with Headings and Lists — Kent State University
sources.claim: Applying Heading styles and using bullets/numbered lists are standard, expected practice for structuring documents.

sources.title: How to Use Bullets and Numbering in Word
sources.claim: Bullets and numbering are core list tools used across reports, resumes, instructions, outlines.

sources.title: Keyboard shortcuts in Word — Microsoft Support
sources.claim: Ctrl+C/V/X, Ctrl+B/I/U, Ctrl+F are the standard everyday shortcuts Microsoft documents first.

subfeature:paste.evidence: CEIP telemetry ranks Paste #1 in Word 2003 (>11% of ALL command use); most-clicked toolbar button.

subfeature:copy.evidence: CEIP telemetry ranks Copy #3 (top-5 ~32% of all command use).

subfeature:cut.evidence: Core clipboard op (Ctrl+X) paired with #1/#3 commands; used less than Paste/Copy.

subfeature:format-painter.evidence: Valued time-saver but a convenience feature below core clipboard/emphasis commands; not in CEIP top ranks.

subfeature:office-clipboard.evidence: 24-item collector pane is a power-user feature most users never open.

feature:clipboard.evidence: Paste (#1), Copy (#3), Cut dominate command usage.

subfeature:bold.evidence: CEIP telemetry ranks Bold #5 — the only text-formatting command in the top five.

subfeature:italic.evidence: One of the three 'workhorse' basic styles (Ctrl+I), just below Bold.

subfeature:underline-gallery.evidence: Core basic text style (Ctrl+U) taught with Bold/Italic.

subfeature:font.evidence: Choosing the typeface is a foundational everyday action every user touches.

subfeature:font-size.evidence: Change Font Size is CEIP #11; setting size is a core basic.

subfeature:font-color-picker.evidence: Standard basic to make text stand out; part of the foundational set.

subfeature:text-highlight-color-picker.evidence: Common for review/emphasis, less universal than font color.

subfeature:change-case.evidence: Handy but occasional; absent from usage rankings and core basics.

subfeature:clear-formatting.evidence: Cleanup command used occasionally; not in top ranks.

subfeature:font-size-increase.evidence: Incremental convenience path; CEIP 'Change Font Size' most plausibly reflects the size box.

subfeature:font-size-decrease.evidence: Secondary incremental control, not a distinct top-usage command.

subfeature:strikethrough.evidence: Niche emphasis style far below bold/italic/underline.

subfeature:font-dialog.evidence: Advanced fallback; most emphasis is done via ribbon buttons/shortcuts.

subfeature:subscript.evidence: Specialized scientific/notation formatting, rare for typical users.

subfeature:text-effects.evidence: Decorative cosmetic extra absent from usage/skill lists.

feature:font.evidence: Bold #5, Change Font Size #11; font/size/emphasis/color are the foundational set.

subfeature:align-left.evidence: Core alignment basic; left is the default/most common.

subfeature:align-justify.evidence: Standard for body text in formal docs, less than left/center.

subfeature:numbering-gallery.evidence: Core list tool for sequenced content, standard for structuring documents.

subfeature:line-spacing.evidence: Important paragraph basic users adjust routinely (single vs double).

subfeature:indent-decrease.evidence: Paired outdent control; used with lists.

subfeature:multilevel-list.evidence: Advanced nested-outline feature; far less than simple bullets/numbering.

subfeature:paragraph-marks.evidence: Troubleshooting aid, not routine document creation.

subfeature:paragraph-dialog.evidence: Fine-grained fallback; everyday adjustments use ribbon buttons.

subfeature:sort.evidence: Niche command absent from usage rankings.

feature:paragraph.evidence: Alignment, lists, line spacing, indents are core everyday formatting.

subfeature:quick-styles.evidence: Applying Heading styles is standard practice (nav pane, auto-TOC); 'one of the most powerful formatting tools.'

subfeature:styles-pane.evidence: Power-user surface; most users apply styles via the ribbon gallery.

feature:styles.evidence: Powerful time-saving tool; standard for headings/consistency/auto-TOC.

subfeature:find.evidence: Ctrl+F is a universal everyday shortcut for locating text.

subfeature:replace.evidence: Common editing tool, less universal than plain Find.

subfeature:select.evidence: Select All is routine; the ribbon menu used less than keyboard selection.

feature:editing.evidence: Find (Ctrl+F, universal) + Replace + Select — routine editing.

notes: Strongest evidence is primary Microsoft CEIP telemetry (Jensen Harris) corroborated by GranneBlog: it fixes an objective ordering for Paste(#1), Copy(#3), Bold(#5), Change Font Size(#11); the curve flattens sharply after the top ~10. Nodes below the top ~11 have no public per-command frequency, graded from that flattening signal + 'essential skills' education sources. Boundary/AI nodes (dictate/editor/create-pdf/office-addins) intentionally have no usage entry -> default 0.25, and are floored to P4 regardless.
